surprises: `--a -Infinity` is an ARGPARSE ERROR (exit 2), not a JSON value, because `-Infinity` fails argparse's negative-number regex `^-\d+$|^-\d*\.\d+$`. Same for `-1e5`, `-1e400`, `-1.`, `-NaN`, `--1`. But `-1`, `-1.5`, `-0.5`, `-.5`, `-12345678901234567890` ARE accepted as values. A naive parser that just takes the next token, or one that rejects every token starting with `-`, gets both halves wrong.

A token starting with `-` is also accepted as a value if it CONTAINS A SPACE (`--a '-1 2'`, `--a '- 1'`) or is exactly `-`. These are argparse's other two escape hatches beyond the negative-number regex.

argparse reports the missing-required error BEFORE the unrecognized-arguments error, so `--A 1 --b true` says `the following arguments are required: --a` and never mentions `--A`. Reimplementations that validate unknown flags first will produce the wrong stderr.

`--` stops option parsing but is ITSELF left in the extras list, so it always shows up in `unrecognized arguments: -- ...`. `--a 1 --b true --` is exit 2, not a successful run. (This is the Python 3.12.5+/3.13 argparse behavior; older argparse silently swallowed the first `--`.)

Long-option abbreviation is on: `--he` and `--hel` invoke help. Also `-h`/`--help` short-circuits before the required-arg check, so `-h --a` prints help with exit 0 rather than erroring on the dangling `--a`.

json.loads accepts `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity` (JSON.parse rejects all three), and rejects the lowercase `nan`/`inf`. It also silently turns `1e400` into +inf, and `1e400` then FAILS `type: integer` while `1.0` PASSES it (Python int-valued-float rule).

Two `NaN` tokens in one document are the same interned Python float object, so `[NaN,NaN]` VIOLATES `uniqueItems: true` even though NaN != NaN. JS's default deep-equal will call them unequal and report 0 errors.
String lengths are code points, not UTF-16 units: `"😀"` (one emoji) satisfies `maxLength: 1`. JS `.length` would say 2.
JSON whitespace is exactly ` \t\n\r`. `\f`, `\v`, U+00A0 and U+2028 are all rejected with `Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)` — U+2028 in particular is a JS-specific gotcha.
Lone/unpaired surrogate escapes (`"\ud800"`, `"\udc00"`, `"\ud83dx"`) are accepted without error by json.loads.
A UTF-8 BOM produces a unique message no other decoder emits: `Unexpected UTF-8 BOM (decode using utf-8-sig): line 1 column 1 (char 0)`.
